questions.q: Where is a custom Apex sharing reason defined declaratively in Setup?
options: On the object's Lightning App Builder page layout
On the custom object's detail page, using the Apex Sharing Reasons related list (Salesforce Classic, or via Metadata/Tooling API)
In Lightning Experience, under the object's Sharing Settings page
Under Setup > Sharing Settings > Sharing Rules
questions.explain: Apex sharing reasons are defined on the custom object's detail page via the Apex Sharing Reasons related list — a screen that still only exists in Salesforce Classic, though it can also be created via the Metadata or Tooling API.

questions.q: A sharing reason is created with the name 'Escalated_Reviewer'. How is it referenced in Apex code?
options: As a custom label resolved at runtime via Label.Escalated_Reviewer
As Object__Share.AccessLevel.Escalated_Reviewer
As the plain string 'Escalated_Reviewer'
As Schema.Object__Share.RowCause.Escalated_Reviewer__c
questions.explain: Salesforce appends __c to the reason's name, and it's referenced through the Schema describe of the share object's RowCause field, giving compile-time safety instead of a hardcoded string.

questions.q: Why would an architect deliberately define two separate Apex sharing reasons (e.g. Escalated_Reviewer__c and Audit_Sample__c) instead of one generic reason for all programmatic sharing?
options: Because a single RowCause value can only be used once per object
So that independent business justifications for access can be tracked and revoked separately, even when they land on the same user
Because each reason corresponds to a different AccessLevel value automatically
Because Salesforce enforces a maximum of one share row per user per record regardless of cause
questions.explain: Multiple reasons let the same user hold independently justified, independently revocable share rows on one record — collapsing them into one generic reason would make it impossible to safely remove one grant without affecting the other.

questions.q: On which objects can a custom Apex sharing reason be defined?
options: Only standard objects that support OWD
Any standard or custom object
Only objects with a master-detail relationship
Only custom objects
questions.explain: Apex sharing reasons can only be defined on custom objects. Programmatic sharing on standard objects relies on the standard causes the platform already provides.

questions.q: What permission must the Apex code's running context have in order to insert, update, or delete Apex managed sharing rows at runtime?
options: Manage Sharing
View All Data
Modify All Data
Author Apex
questions.explain: Only a running context with Modify All Data can create or change Apex managed sharing rows — ordinarily satisfied by running the logic in a system context such as a trigger handler rather than depending on the individual user's permissions.
